pr.body: Updated client.js to omit cursor on the initial request, pass each returned cursor unchanged on subsequent requests, and append page items in order. README.md documents pagination; test/client.test.js covers cursor forwarding, order, and absent/null termination. Final npm test passed (5/5); git diff --check passed. Assumes API responses include items and optionally next_cursor as specified.
pr.summary: listItems now follows pagination cursors and returns all items in API order. Before: returned the first page only; now: collects pages until next_cursor is null or absent.

evidence.caption: Before, GET /items returned all 57 items and only an items key; after, default limit is 20 and next_cursor is returned. The final unittest suite passes.

pr.body: Implemented limit validation (1–100, default 20), ID-based cursor validation and continuation, and the {items, next_cursor} response in api.py. Updated README.md and added pagination, traversal, and invalid parameter tests in test_api.py. Verification: python3 -m unittest (5 tests, passed); git diff --check (passed). Cursor strings are decimal item IDs returned unchanged by the API. The change is a contained public API behavior change.
pr.summary: Added bounded cursor pagination to GET /items. Before: all 57 records returned at once; now: clients can fetch ordered pages of up to 100 items with a returned cursor and null on the final page.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to items endpoint

risk.why: Contained behavior change to GET /items in api.py with supporting README and tests; no persistence, concurrency, security, or migration changes. The response shape changes from an unpaginated object to the specified envelope. Full unittest suite and diff check pass.
